Every result below was produced in this environment on the date above. None of
it is quoted from an earlier bundle. The official 532 GB checkpoint was not
present, so nothing here is official-weight parity.

Correction: the 2026-08-02 revision of this file recorded tree
bd7c8750100d393c13cd36062489cc4fce27ad69 and was not regenerated when the
official-transformers layer parity landed, so it named a tree two changes
behind the bundle it shipped beside. The hashes below were produced by the run
that produced this file.

GENERATION
----------
PASS  integration/waste/generate.sh reproduces the reviewed v18 tree
      Result: ce6c5272e801c651cc6b71f869a1b0cd7167dab5, byte-identical to the
      tree produced by `git am` of waste-inkling-patch-v18. Established before
      any source change, as the correctness check on the extraction itself.

PASS  integration/waste/generate.sh is deterministic on a fixed toolchain
      Two independent runs over identical sources produced identical patch
      bytes.

      Qualified after CI disproved the unqualified claim: `git format-patch`
      ends the file with the LOCAL Git version, so a runner on Git 2.54.0
      produced different bytes from this host's 2.43.0 with nothing stale.
      The generator now passes --no-signature, and the CI gate compares the
      APPLIED TREE HASH rather than patch bytes — content-addressed, immune to
      toolchain drift, and identical to what a consumer relies on.

PASS  committed bundle applies to the reviewed tree
      git am of dist/waste-inkling-6931570/patches/*.patch onto the pinned
      upstream yields 9a2b768986d4cbedb3cfc5944c6c229d7264f884.
      Patch sha256: a7a2ff1198daa0ee78709c8bc2fabf13acb85ae39bee1b7bae66f7f95cfabb4f

PASS  complete Inkling Python suite
      python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ink*.py" -t .
      Result: 179 tests, OK, process exit 0
      python3 -m unittest tests.test_inspect_inkling tests.test_convert_inkling
      Result: 18 tests, OK
      Total: 197 tests passing.

      The v16 bundle recorded 99 tests and nothing re-ran them; that number is
      confirmed, and the fixture reader, the layer-parity harness, the
      official-transformers layer comparison, and the decode cost model bring
      the total to 197.

      The process exit code is checked deliberately. An earlier revision of
      inkling_layer_parity.py declared waste_inkling_attention_state with six
      fields where the header has eleven, so every state_init wrote 88 bytes
      into a 64-byte buffer. All tests passed and the numbers were correct; the
      interpreter segfaulted during shutdown garbage collection. A suite that
      only reads "OK" would have shipped it.

PASS  ctypes struct layout probe
      tests/test_inkling_layer_parity.py compiles a C probe that prints
      sizeof() for the attention state, layer state, layer scratch, layer
      weights, and config, and compares each against ctypes.sizeof.
      Verified to fail on the six-field declaration above.

PASS  dependency-light selection, no torch installed
      tests/test_inspect_inkling.py, tests/test_inkling_plan.py,

PASS  python3 -m compileall -q tools tests

PASS  Windows cross-build and execution
      Toolchain: x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-posix 13.2.0, run under Wine 9.0
      - all 12 Inkling translation units compiled -Werror for the target
      - full `make CC=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-posix` produced waste.exe and
        libwaste.dll
      - test_inkling.exe  -> INKLING OK
      - test_inkling_io.exe -> INKLING IO OK
      - waste.exe plan on an Inkling container produced byte-identical
        figures to the Linux build

      This is the first time inkling_stage_reader.c's Windows branch has been
      compiled by anything, let alone run. It carries a complete second
      positional-read implementation (ReadFile with OVERLAPPED) that the
      Python differential tests cannot reach and that no CI job touched.
      test_inkling_io.c exists so that one binary exercises it on both
      platforms.

      NOT claimed: native Windows. This is a cross-build executed under Wine.
      Offsets above 4 GiB, NTFS atomic replacement, Unicode paths, and
      cancellation during a multi-hundred-GB conversion remain untested.

I/O MEASUREMENT, AND A BUG IT FOUND
-----------------------------------
PASS  tools/diskbench.c now bypasses the page cache on Linux
      Until this bundle, nocache() was #ifdef __APPLE__ with no Linux arm and
      no open() used O_DIRECT, so every Linux run measured the page cache
      whenever the file fit in RAM — and printed it under the label
      "cache bypassed". That is the fiction upstream's GATES.md Gate 5 exists
      to prevent, defeated on one platform by a missing #else.

      Same host, same 8 GiB file, same 9,457,664 B Inkling record:

                        unpatched   with O_DIRECT   inflation
        seq read        5.66 GiB/s     2.39 GiB/s        2.4x
        rand 1 thread   5.67 GiB/s     2.08 GiB/s        2.7x
        rand 2 threads  8.41 GiB/s     2.41 GiB/s        3.5x
        rand 4 threads 14.49 GiB/s     3.00 GiB/s        4.8x

      The unpatched figure is higher than the 12.89 GiB/s upstream measured on
      an M5 Pro internal SSD, on a cloud VM that really does 3.00.

      A refused O_DIRECT is now reported rather than silently downgraded, and
      the trailing tok/s column takes the model's GB/token instead of
      hardcoding K3's 12.5.

      NOT claimed: that these are laptop numbers. This host is a cloud VM on
      virtio. 2.08 GiB/s at queue depth 1 is a slow modern NVMe.

PASS  decode cost model
      tools/inkling_throughput.py, 45 tests. Geometry is exact and checked
      against a record inkling_vq.write_expert_record actually writes:
      9,457,664 B per routed expert, 240 records and 2.11 GiB per decoded
      token, a 90.20 GiB expert bank.

      Throughput is a PROJECTION, labelled as one in every line it prints. It
      is calibrated against upstream's measured K3 decomposition and reproduces
      K3's own measured decode (0.61 tok/s against a measured 0.56-0.63) before
      being applied to Inkling. See docs/THROUGHPUT.md §5 for the four things
      that would falsify it.

PUBLIC SURFACE PROMOTED
-----------------------
waste_plan_memory() now answers for an Inkling container; waste_open and
everything downstream still return WASTE_E_UNSUPPORTED.

The promotion is scoped to planning on purpose. A plan is arithmetic over
declared geometry, so a bug in it produces a wrong byte count that the caller
sees immediately. A forward pass is a claim about a model whose official
weights this code has never read.

Cross-checks against the geometry documented in docs/INKLING.md, on a
synthetic Inkling manifest carrying the released Small config:
  KV + four convolution rings at 4K ctx   371 MB   (predicted 0.362 GiB)
  minimum expert cache                    108 MB   (6 x 9,457,664 x 2)
  resident trunk excludes both row-backed vocabulary tables

WHAT IS STILL NOT CLAIMED
-------------------------
Official-weight activation parity has not run: the checkpoint was not present.
Tokenizer, chat template, serving, multimodal execution, native Windows, and
production performance all remain gates. The public loader still returns
WASTE_E_UNSUPPORTED for any Inkling container, by design.
